# Third-Party Notices

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/third-party-notices.ts from guideline-registry.yaml and the checklist licence headers. Do not edit by hand; run `bun run docs:third-party-notices`. -->

Methodsmith is MIT-licensed. The reporting-guideline checklists bundled under `plugins/methodsmith/skills/method-review/references/` adapt third-party guideline material, each under its own terms. This file records the licence status and how each checklist's text is used, derived from the [guideline registry](https://github.com/sajor2000/methodsmith/blob/main/plugins/methodsmith/skills/method-review/references/guideline-registry.yaml) and each checklist's source-and-licence header; registry verification date 2026-10-19.

No guideline source documents (PDFs, Word files, supplements) are redistributed. Where the effective licence of quoted text is open (CC BY, CC0, public domain), item text is quoted verbatim with attribution; where a source is restricted or unlicensed, item text is a faithful paraphrase. A mixed case (open-licence checklist inside a restricted article) follows its checklist header, quoted in full below. The "What to look for" review cues in each checklist are methodsmith's own and are not guideline content. For verbatim wording of any restricted source, consult the official publication cited in each checklist and in `docs/guideline-sources.md`.

Coverage: 49 bundled checklists — 19 quote item text verbatim under open terms, 30 are faithful paraphrases or adaptations.

## Restricted or mixed-licence sources

Item text from these sources is paraphrased unless the entry's own statement says the quoted checklist carries an open licence (mixed case).
- **CARE** (CARE Guidelines; doi:10.7453/gahmj.2013.008) — CC BY-NC-ND (non-commercial, no derivatives) + All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > The article is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 and the checklist files state no open licence, so item descriptions are faithful paraphrases of the official checklist rather than verbatim text. The "What to look for" bullets are added by this plugin.
- **CHART** (CHART statement; doi:10.1186/s12916-025-04274-w) — CC BY-NC-ND (non-commercial, no derivatives).
  > The BMC Medicine article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which allows neither commercial reuse nor adapted versions, so item text below is a faithful paraphrase of Table 2; item and subitem numbers and headings are exact. Review cues are added by this plugin.
- **CLAIM** (CLAIM 2024 update; doi:10.1148/ryai.240300) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > The article is © 2024 Radiological Society of North America and is not openly licensed. Item numbers and short item titles are reproduced; descriptions are faithful paraphrases of the article's guidance, not verbatim text. Review cues are added by this plugin.
- **CONSORT-CLUSTER** (CONSORT cluster extension; doi:10.1136/bmj.e5661) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > The BMJ article and the checklist file state no open licence, so the item descriptions below are close paraphrases of the official extension text. They keep each item's meaning and qualifiers but are not verbatim; consult the source for exact wording. The "What to look for" bullets and the CONSORT 2025 mapping lines are added by this plugin.
- **CONSORT-NOF1** (CENT 2015 statement; doi:10.1136/bmj.h1738) — CC BY-NC (non-commercial) + CC BY 4.0 + All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > Checklist text reproduced verbatim (including its original punctuation) from the CENT 2015 checklist, which states: "The copyright for CENT (including checklist) is held by the CENT Group and is distributed under a Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY 4.0) license." (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The BMJ article itself is CC BY-NC 4.0. The CC BY statement is a footnote to the checklist (Table 1), so the abstract guidance (Table 2) is treated as part of the CC BY-NC article and paraphrased. The "What to look for" bullets and the CONSORT 2025 mapping lines are added by this plugin and are not CENT text.
- **CONSORT-OUT** (CONSORT-Outcomes 2022 extension; doi:10.1001/jama.2022.21022) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > All 17 extension item IDs and their CONSORT-section mapping were verified on 2026-10-19 against Table 1 of the JAMA paper, which interleaves the extension items with the core items of CONSORT 2010, which CONSORT 2025 supersedes. The JAMA article is copyright 2022 American Medical Association (all rights reserved) and carries no open licence (checked 2026-10-19 via Crossref and the published PDF), so the item descriptions below are faithful paraphrases that keep every element of the official item. Use the JAMA paper or the CONSORT website's fillable checklist for verbatim wording. The "What to look for" bullets are methodsmith review guidance, not CONSORT-Outcomes 2022 content.
- **COREQ** (COREQ; doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzm042) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > Item numbers, domains, and item names follow Table 1 of Tong et al. 2007 (https://doi.org/10.1093/intqhc/mzm042). Verified against the original article on 2026-10-15: all 32 items, the 3 domains, and the 8 subsections match Table 1 in number, name, and order, and each paraphrase keeps every element of the guide question. That article is copyright Oxford University Press and is not openly licensed, so each description is a faithful paraphrase of the published guide question, not a verbatim copy. EQUATOR record: https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/coreq/. COREQ is scoped to interviews and focus groups; an LLM extension (COREQ+LLM) is in development (Fehring L, et al. JMIR Res Protoc. 2025;14:e78682. PMID: 40991937) and has no final checklist yet. The "What to look for" bullets are methodsmith review guidance, not part of the guideline.
- **DEAL** (DEAL checklist (Development, Evaluation, and Assessment of Large Language Models; DEAL-A/DEAL-B); doi:10.1056/AIp2401106) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > The article is published by NEJM Group (Massachusetts Medical Society) and the appendix ("provided by the authors") carries no open licence. Item IDs and item names are kept as published so findings can cite them; every description is a faithful paraphrase that keeps each element of the official item and adds nothing. Use the official appendix for verbatim wording. The pathway definitions are quoted from the EQUATOR record. The review cues are added by this plugin and are not DEAL text.
- **DECIDE-AI** (DECIDE-AI; doi:10.1038/s41591-022-01772-9) — CC BY-NC (non-commercial).
  > The BMJ version is CC BY-NC 4.0 (no commercial reuse), so items are faithful paraphrases of Table 2; item numbers and themes are exact.
- **GRAMMS** (GRAMMS (Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study); doi:10.1258/jhsrp.2007.007074) — CC BY 4.0 + All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > Item numbers and content follow the six GRAMMS items in O'Cathain et al. 2008. The article is copyright SAGE and is not openly licensed, and its full text was not accessible during verification, so each description is a faithful paraphrase of the published item. On 2026-10-15 the six items were cross-checked against the GRAMMS update protocol (Munce S, et al. JMIR Res Protoc. 2026;15:e82364. doi:10.2196/82364. PMID: 41841629; CC BY 4.0), which lists the six components in the same order and with the same content but in its own sentence, not as a quotation, so it does not confirm the original wording. The original wording remains UNVERIFIED against the 2008 article. Journal-hosted GRAMMS checklists were also consulted, including an author-supplied GRAMMS checklist in the supplement to Pieterse P, Saracini F. BMJ Glob Health. 2025;10:e021043 (doi:10.1136/bmjgh-2025-021043; checked 2026-10-15). That copy lists the six items in the same order and with wording matching the update protocol's list, except for a typo in item 5 ("present" for "presence"). It is secondary corroboration, not the primary source. EQUATOR record (acronym GRAMMS): https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/the-quality-of-mixed-methods-studies-in-health-services-research/. An update, GRAMMS 2.0, is in development (protocol published 17 March 2026 and registered with EQUATOR: methodological review, modified Delphi survey, then consensus meeting); no updated checklist exists yet, so the 2008 items remain current. The "What to look for" bullets are methodsmith review guidance, not part of the guideline.
- **MI-CLAIM** (MI-CLAIM checklist; doi:10.1038/s41591-020-1041-y) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > The PMC copy is an NIH author manuscript (fair use, not openly licensed), so items are faithful paraphrases of Table 1.
- **PDSQI-9** (Provider Documentation Summarization Quality Instrument (PDSQI-9); doi:10.1093/jamia/ocaf068) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > Attribute names follow Table 1 of Croxford et al. 2025. The article is copyright Oxford University Press (all rights reserved), so each definition below is a faithful paraphrase, not a verbatim copy. Consult the publication for the exact rating instructions and scales.
- **PRISMA-DTA** (PRISMA-DTA; doi:10.1001/jama.2017.19163) — All rights reserved / no open licence.
  > Item IDs and order follow the official PRISMA-DTA checklist (https://www.prisma-statement.org/s/PRISMA-DTA-Checklist-xh5j.pdf). That checklist carries no open licence, so the descriptions are faithful paraphrases: every element of each official item is kept and nothing is added. Use the official PDF for verbatim wording.
